slot_scores.name: exact_demand_equality
slot_scores.evidence_quote: Should the model require that all 8500 demand slots be filled exactly (i.e., every branch-specialty demand is met), or is it acceptable to leave some demand slots unfilled?
slot_scores.rationale: The agent explicitly asked whether demand must be met exactly or whether slots may be left unfilled, covering the exact-equality vs lower-bound distinction.

slot_scores.name: priority_order_lexicographic
slot_scores.evidence_quote: Should this be a separate minimization objective ... as the third priority (p3), after fully meeting demand (p1) and maximizing the number meeting their preferred specialty (p2).
slot_scores.rationale: The agent explicitly asked about the priority hierarchy and framed p3 as coming after p1 and p2, which targets the lexicographic/preemptive ordering.

stopping_behavior.rationale: Both P0/P1 hidden slots were resolved by turn 4, but the agent continued with many repetitive, low-value questions from turns 5 through 30, including near-identical repeated questions about preferred specialty and preferred city counting.

summary: The agent recovered the key hidden facts on exact demand fulfillment and lexicographic priority early, but then engaged in excessive repetitive questioning that added little new information.

restoration_summary.rule: Exact restoration uses only P0/P1 slots; unresolved P2 slots do not affect exact restoration.

stopping_consistency_audit.rule: Any non-yes P0/P1 slot at READY_TO_MODEL is unresolved.
